scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes the material specifications, design configurations, nominal sizes, mechanical clearances, performance tests, and criteria for conformity for mortice night latches used for general domestic and commercial building security applications [1].

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Mechanical Engineering Department / Utensils, Cutlery and Domestic Hardware)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to obtain a valid BIS license to stamp or etch the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' directly on the latch body, cover, or packaging to demonstrate metallurgical and non-interchangeability compliance in the building materials sector.

requirements.detail: Final observed or calculated test and analytical values (such as clearances, sizes, and specific test limits) must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard [3].
Mortice night latches fitted with two levers must be manufactured with non-interchangeable keys in standard production batches of at least 12 latches [1].
To verify key uniqueness, exactly 3 latches are selected from each batch of 12 (with slightly differing key wards). If any key opens another lock, the entire batch lot must be rejected [1].
Mortice night latches fitted with more than two levers must be manufactured with non-interchangeable keys in standard production batches of at least 60 latches [1].
For key verification on multi-lever batches, exactly 5 latches are selected from each batch of 60. The entire lot is rejected if any key cross-opens another lock [1].

The rectangular locking bolt (spring bolt) must be fabricated from robust metals (such as cast or extruded brass) and feature a section of not less than 8 mm x 25 mm to prevent structural warping and break-ins.
The total depth of the lock body case must not exceed 15 mm to ensure it can be morticed into standard timber door stiles without compromising shutter strength.
Any latch failing to satisfy material, dimensional, key operation, handle retraction, or corrosion-plating requirements is defined as a defective unit [2].

The entire manufacturing batch is declared conforming to IS 3847 if the number of defective units found during sample inspections does not exceed the allowable limit specified in Column 3 of Table 2 [2].

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 3847 : 1992 (First Revision, Reaffirmed 2021) is the primary national Indian Standard specification prescribing construction, dimensional, material, and safety requirements for mechanically operated mortice night latches. Maintained under MED 33, the code unifies residential and commercial door security hardware in India. It defines night latches as spring-bolt locks operated by key outside, handle inside, and fitted with an internal key-lockout snib [1]. It restricts lock case depth to 15 mm to prevent weakening timber doors, specifies a minimum 8 mm x 25 mm bolt section, and enforces strict key non-interchangeability batches (at least 12 for two-lever and 60 for multi-lever locks) [1]. The standard mandates regular sampling and testing to eliminate defective units and coordinate directly with door framing (IS 1003) and paint/safety codes [2].
